characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; 5 repeated measurements averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: To measure the Vickers hardness of the aged 17Al samples

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 17Al 650 °C/1 h SE image shows a uniform matrix with fine 'New precipitates' pointed out (magenta arrows) in the 10 µm inset.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 17Al alloy after aging at 650 °C for 1 h; 50 µm main-panel scale bar with a 10 µm inset
characterization_methods.purpose: To identify the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) and fine new precipitates in the aged samples

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting raw materials of high purity (>99.9 %) in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates of 4 mm thickness.
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples using electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq).
Solution-treated samples aged between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h, followed by water quenching; this sample corresponds to 650 °C for 1 h.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness: load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the value given as the average of 5 measurements.

phases_present.morphology: matrix formed by the almost complete α→β-Mn transformation

precipitates.distribution: within the β-Mn / at β-Mn interfaces

structures.overall_structure: After aging the 17Al alloy at 650 °C for 1 h, the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn (at 600 °C and above the α→β-Mn transformation in the 17Al alloy is complete within just 1 h of aging). Numerous fine new precipitates (BCC and FCC Cu-rich phases) are distributed within the β-Mn. SE-SEM of the 650 °C/1 h condition shows a uniform matrix with fine 'New precipitates' resolved in the 10 µm inset.

unmapped_findings: EDS-measured chemical composition of the 17Al alloy (at.%): Fe 43.2, Mn 34.8, Al 17.0, Cu 5.0 (Table 1).
Nominal composition of the studied alloy series is Fe-35Mn-xAl-5Cu (at.%, x = 15, 17, 19); the 17Al alloy (this sample's alloy) has nominal 17 at.% Al.

Density of the 17Al alloy measured by the Archimedes method is 6.76 g·cm⁻³ (note: the highest specific hardness of 141 HV·cm³/g reported in the paper belongs to the 15Al alloy, not to this 17Al sample).
